name: Oregon Trunk Railway
description: Oregon Trunk Railway was an SP&S-system railroad serving central Oregon. Diesel operation began around 1948 with SP&S/Great Northern-supplied locomotives; its operations entered Burlington Northern in 1970.

history: Diesel operation on Oregon Trunk began around 1948. By January 1, 1950, Spokane, Portland and Seattle Railway supplied all Oregon Trunk motive power. Equipment operated over the line was not necessarily owned by Oregon Trunk.

In 1947, traffic averaged about 4.4 freight trains per day with an average of 61 cars per train. This traffic scale supports the project’s operating-equivalent equipment estimates; the estimates are not reported owned-fleet totals.

1969 was the final full operating year before Oregon Trunk ceased separate railroad-employer status on March 3, 1970, as operations came under Burlington Northern control. Burlington Northern is its operational successor; the Oregon Trunk corporate entity continued afterward as a BN subsidiary.
paintSchemesIntro: Oregon Trunk did not maintain a distinct diesel locomotive paint scheme. Diesel motive power was supplied by Spokane, Portland and Seattle Railway and retained SP&S paint, lettering and numbers.
